reason: Hypothesis A directly addresses the research question by targeting grain-boundary strengthening in MoNbTaW, the only alloy class shown to survive 1600°C tests, with a specific, testable mechanism (boron segregation/pinning) and a clear falsification experiment, whereas Hypothesis B proposes a generic oxide-dispersion approach without linking to the specific alloy or temperature regime (900–1100°C vs. the 1200–1600°C jet-turbine target) and lacks supporting evidence for this material system.
